evidence: The hunk shows `if (opts.config)` as the exclusivity guard, so `--config=` yields '' and skips it exactly as claimed. Rejecting empties at the parse boundary was a sound alternative to N `!== undefined` rewrites, but applying it to every option in `known` was over-broad and produced F7.
guidance_note: Before moving a check to a parse boundary that covers every option, list each option and what an empty value means for it, and apply the rejection only where empty is genuinely illegal.

evidence: resolveConfigChain was new two-branch logic, it was not exported, and nothing tested it. dcffb0f exports it and adds fixture tests for the file branch, --use ordering, and the preset branch.
guidance_note: When adding a new branching function whose output drives main(), export it and test each branch in the same commit.

evidence: `config.model.split('/').slice(1).join('/')` on a bare model name gives '' and emits `models: { '': {} }`. The throw-in-adapter fix is the right call, but the throw sits inside materializeHome after mkdtempSync, and that placement leaked the temp dir (F6).
guidance_note: When adding a throw to a builder, trace its callers for resources already acquired (temp dirs, handles) and make sure they are released on the new throw path.

evidence: The original code set `const config = chain[0]` and passed it to formatReport even though runMultiScope returns configUsed after failover. dcffb0f destructures configUsed and passes it through, matching run.js.
guidance_note: When a change turns a single-element input into a real failover chain, grep for every consumer of chain[0] and switch the post-run ones to the result's configUsed.

evidence: The cli.js comment said '(no per-engine read grant needed)' while this PR added `external_directory: 'allow'` to opencode. dcffb0f amends the comment to name the exception.
guidance_note: When adding an exception to a shared design invariant, grep for the comment that states the invariant and amend it in the same commit.

evidence: dcffb0f added `throw new Error("opencode requires a '<provider>/<model>' ...")` inside buildOpencodeConfig. That runs from materializeHome after mkdtempSync, so the throw abandons the temp home before cli.js's finally can see it, a leak path that did not exist before the fix. The agent took the reviewer's try/catch option and widened it to every throw in the function.
guidance_note: When the fix for a finding introduces a new throw, check what the enclosing function has already allocated and release it on that path before pushing.

evidence: dcffb0f's `if (value === '') throw` applies to every option in `known`, so `--scope "$SCOPE"` with SCOPE unset, which used to run, now hard-fails. The fix scoped the rejection to a NON_EMPTY_OPTIONS set of the two-source options.
guidance_note: When a fix generalizes a reviewer's single-option concern to all options, check the generalization against the options whose empty value is a legitimate default before pushing.

narrative: Round 0 raised five real issues, and the agent accepted all of them in one commit, dcffb0f. Two of those fixes created the only round-1 findings. The parse-boundary empty-value rejection was applied to every option and broke --scope/--repo (F7). The opencode model-shape throw landed after mkdtempSync and leaked the temp home (F6). Both were fixed cleanly in 987be3f, so round 2 exists only because of the round-0 fixes.
guidance_observations: Both fix-caused findings came from generalizing or relocating a fix past what the reviewer asked for, without checking the side effects of the wider scope.
The agent filed the identical pre-existing leak in the codex/claude-code adapters as a separate ticket instead of widening the PR, which kept scope in bounds.

evidence: The diff does replace the read-in-full instruction with 'Judge each change from its diff hunk alone', but the PR is titled 'DO NOT MERGE — eval CI gate validation (sabotaged worker prompt)', so the reviewer's 'accidental inclusion' diagnosis is wrong. The PR was closed unmerged; silence on a throwaway branch cost nothing, but a one-line note that the change is intentional would have closed the thread.

The charter inversion ('false alarm is far more expensive than a miss') is real, but it is the deliberate sabotage the PR title announces, not a shipping bug. The PR closed unmerged per the 2026-09-06 issue comment.

It is accurate that readTargets is now unreferenced and that the scout's 'reads in full' promise is contradicted, but both follow from the intentional sabotage edit on a DO-NOT-MERGE branch. They are not defects to fix.
The contradiction between the new threshold and the unchanged severity tiers is real, but it is what a deliberately degraded prompt looks like. The branch was never meant to merge.
This is a repeat of F2 after the rebase onto #133. The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: f74821f is the sabotage commit itself, rebased, not a fix for any finding.

The claim rests on compare.js's verdict-write try/catch only warning, and compare.js is not in the packet. eval.yml merged via #133 (bec2705), so this finding on live workflow code was never routed anywhere. The flag is a false positive because f74821f touches only src/prompt.js.
This is a repeat of F4 after the rebase. The flag is a false positive because f74821f is the intentional sabotage commit, not a review fix.

This is a repeat of F1/F3, with the readTargets dead code and the removed full-context check. Both are accurate descriptions of an intentional DO-NOT-MERGE sabotage. The flag is a false positive because f74821f is the sabotage commit rebased.

The contradiction with the unshowable-files note and the dependency Grep instruction is plausibly real, but it is a consequence of the intended sabotage on a branch closed unmerged. The flag is a false positive for the same reason as F5.

The finding sets the README's 'uploaded ... even on a red or aborted run' against an eval.yml:106-107 comment that this packet does not show. The README text merged via #133, so a true finding went unaddressed. The flag is a false positive because f74821f touches only src/prompt.js.

It is true that the shared reviewCharter's 'obvious in the diff hunk' clause is unsatisfiable in whole-repo mode, but this is part of the deliberate sabotage text. The flag is a false positive for the same reason as F5.

narrative: This was a deliberately sabotaged DO-NOT-MERGE PR whose purpose was to prove the eval gate reds a degraded engine. It was closed unmerged on 2026-09-06. Nine of the eleven findings correctly describe the sabotage but misdiagnose it as accidental. Round 1 re-raised them because the sabotage commit was rebased, not because of any fix. The two eval.yml/README findings (F6, F10) target content that did merge via #133, and nobody replied to or ticketed them.
guidance_observations: A validation PR whose branch carries content that also lands elsewhere should still route reviewer findings on the shared files to the merged PR or a ticket; F6 and F10 were dropped.
A one-line PR-level note telling the reviewer the prompt change is intentional would have avoided paying for a second full review round.

evidence: '~$3.50 and ~1 hour' was hand-typed into both the workflow header and the README while compare.js computes the real estimate. ecff19e removes the dollar figure from the workflow and leaves the README with an attributed order-of-magnitude.
guidance_note: Do not hand-copy a figure a tool computes at runtime into comments; point at the tool's output instead.

evidence: GitHub withholds secrets from fork pull_request events, so a labeled fork PR would run with empty credentials. ecff19e adds `head.repo.full_name == github.repository` to the job if, which is the restriction option the reviewer offered.
guidance_note: When writing a secret-consuming pull_request workflow, gate it on same-repo PRs from the start.

evidence: The workflow forwards only DEEPSEEK/ZAI/OPENAI keys, yet both the comment and the README claimed 'all provider credentials the action accepts', and the action also accepts CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. ecff19e narrows both to the run-case.js set.
guidance_note: Write completeness claims ('every', 'all') against the actual enumerated list, not the intent.

evidence: ecff19e rewrote the README credential sentence to mirror the workflow comment's 'pinned provider' explanation but dropped the comment's second clause, 'DEEPSEEK_API_KEY also serves the default llm matcher's judge'. The README rationale was left incomplete in a way a maintainer re-pinning cases could act on.
guidance_note: When rewriting one copy of a statement to match another, carry over every clause of the source, not just the one the finding named.

narrative: Round 0 raised three valid doc and workflow findings, all accepted and fixed in ecff19e. Round 1's single finding came from the F3 fix: it rewrote the README credential sentence but omitted the DEEPSEEK judge clause that the workflow comment it was mirroring carried. Fixing that in f70eb98 produced approval in round 2.
guidance_observations: The workflow comment and the README stated the same facts twice, so every fix had to be applied to both copies, and the round-1 finding is that drift.

evidence: The original runScopeWorkers set `{ status: 'unreviewed' }` on DeadlineExceededError and never read e.span, so the span the PR stamped had no consumer. f26b6b4 carries it as a span-only usage and folds it through sumUsage.
guidance_note: When adding a field to an error 'for upstream callers', trace every catch site that absorbs that error and wire the consumer in the same commit.

evidence: f26b6b4 added `usage` to both 'unreviewed' outcome branches but left the pool's return-type comment reading `{ status: 'unreviewed' }`.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a field to a discriminated value, update the type comment that documents that union in the same commit.

evidence: The span-only usage shape and its renderCostLine test were in the original PR, and f26b6b4 does not touch usage.js or its tests, so the flag is a false positive. The gap was the original PR leaving the costMarker/parseCostRecord persistence path without a round-trip test.
guidance_note: When introducing a new value shape, add a round-trip test for every persistence path that serializes that value, not just the render paths.

evidence: F1's fix wired err.span into the deadline-kill consumer, but retryTransientSpawn, another catcher of span-bearing errors, still drops failed attempts' spans. The agent took the reviewer's 'narrow the claim' option and ticketed the fold to zai-timing-31d.5, which #135 then implemented.
guidance_note: When fixing one consumer that drops a propagated field, grep every catch of that error type (retry loops included) and fix or document each in the same commit.

evidence: In the cli.js hunk, `span` is in scope after runEngine, but a throw from extractUsage or readCollectedReview (a ProtocolError) loses it. This is the same 'span stamped but lost before aggregation' class that F1's fix addressed for the deadline path; cli.js itself was not touched by f26b6b4.
guidance_note: When establishing an invariant like 'every post-spawn rejection carries its span', enumerate every throw site after the spawn, across files, not just the helper that stamps it.

narrative: Round 0 found that the stamped err.span had no consumer on the deadline-kill path. f26b6b4 wired that one consumer but left the type comment stale (F2), and round 1 found two more places the same span was dropped: the retry loop (F4) and cli.js post-spawn throws (F5). Round 1 also found an independent missing persistence test (F3), so round 2 would have happened regardless. All round-1 findings were fixed or properly ticketed in 328c079.
guidance_observations: The PR claimed 'no outcome loses its duration' without enumerating the outcomes; doing that sweep before round 0 or in the F1 fix would have surfaced F4 and F5 together.
Deferring the retry-attempt fold to the next ticket while narrowing the comment now was a sound scope call, and #135 delivered it.

evidence: In the original describeSchedule, `if (s.phase !== 'worker') continue` silently drops unknown phases, and nothing linked the producer's record shape to the consumer. ee6998c adds a validating spawnRecord mint and exhaustive phase dispatch, but covers only the inner record, even though the finding named the schedule shape too (see F3).
guidance_note: When a finding names a shape crossing a module boundary, give every level of that shape (inner record and outer envelope) a single owner in the same fix.

evidence: sweepCap was validated at runMultiScopePass entry but maxConcurrent was not, and describeSchedule divides by it. ee6998c adds the positive-integer gate beside sweepCap's, the reviewer's first option.
guidance_note: When recording a parameter that a later derivation divides by, validate it at the same entry gate as its sibling parameters.

evidence: F1 flagged 'the SpawnRecord/schedule shape'. ee6998c minted only the inner SpawnRecord through spawnRecord and left `schedule: { scopeConcurrency, sweepCap, scopeCount, spawns }` as a bare literal. 424eb43 added scheduleRecord for the outer envelope.
guidance_note: When fixing a shape-ownership finding, list every object literal that crosses the same boundary and route all of them through the new owner.

evidence: `wavesPerPass = Math.ceil(scopeCount / scopeConcurrency)` is already in the original commit (shown in F2's hunk) and ee6998c does not change it, so the ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive. The bug is real: a partially refused pass reports planned waves, contradicting the comment's 'work that actually ran'.
guidance_note: When a comment claims a derived figure reflects actual work, test the derivation against the partial-execution case (budget cut mid-pass), not just the all-or-nothing ones.

evidence: ee6998c, F1's fix, wrote the header saying describeSchedule 'dispatches exhaustively on the same vocabulary — so ... a new outcome value fails loudly at the mint or the derive', but the derive branches only on phase and copies outcome through unchecked. Narrowing the comment (the reviewer's second option) was the right call over adding a second enforcer.
guidance_note: When writing a guarantee comment alongside a fix, check each clause against the code the fix actually added, field by field.

narrative: Round 0's shape-ownership finding (F1) was fixed for the inner SpawnRecord only, and round 1 flagged the outer schedule envelope (F3). Round 1 also flagged a pre-existing wave-count bug on partially refused passes (F4). The F1 fix's header comment overclaimed outcome validation at the derive, which cost round 2 (F5). Round 3 approved after a comment-only fix.
guidance_observations: Both fix-caused findings trace to one fix commit (ee6998c) that implemented less than its own comment and the finding's wording claimed; checking the fix against the finding text and its own new comments would have saved a round.

evidence: The hunk interpolates `${s.scope}` raw into a markdown table row and the slowest-scope clause, and scope names are LLM-minted strings. 4232be6 adds a renderer-owned scopeText escape for both sites. The agent cited one-way-deps to explain why it did not import dependency-diff.js's escape, which fits since schedule.js is dependency-free.
guidance_note: When rendering any model-generated string into markdown or HTML, escape it at every interpolation site in the first commit.

evidence: run.js wraps renderTimingBreakdown in try/catch, but the local-review.js call `const timing = renderTimingBreakdown(...)` is unguarded, so a throw aborts the whole report. 4232be6 wraps it and prints 'timing: unavailable (<cause>)'.
guidance_note: When reusing a renderer that one call site deliberately guards, apply the same guard at every new call site.

evidence: The hunk adds `scouts` to describeSchedule's return value, but the 'Returns {...}' block above the function does not list it.
guidance_note: When adding a field to a function's return value, update its documented return shape in the same edit.

evidence: `Date.parse(span.to) - Date.parse(span.from)` can be negative or NaN, and that value now reaches a PR-facing footer. Mapping both to null at spanMs reuses the existing 'unclocked' rendering instead of making one bad span throw away the whole breakdown, which is a better fix than validating in formatMs.
guidance_note: When a value first becomes user-visible, check the computation that produces it for out-of-domain results (negative or NaN durations) and map them at that boundary.

narrative: Round 0 raised four real issues: unescaped LLM scope names, an unguarded local render, a stale return-shape comment, and negative or NaN spans reaching the footer. All four were fixed in one commit, with a better-placed different fix for the span domain. Round 1 approved with no fix-caused findings.
guidance_observations: The PR guarded the production render site but not the dev-script render site of the same function; checking all call sites of a newly guarded call would have prevented F2.

evidence: renderRunningTotal formats `now() - startedAt` with no negative or NaN screen, unlike spanMs, which #136 had already guarded. 56b9563 extracts an asDuration predicate that both use, matching the reviewer's 'null it out the same way spanMs does'.
guidance_note: When computing a new duration in a module that already owns a duration-validity predicate, route the new value through that predicate instead of passing it straight to the formatter.

narrative: There was a single finding: a new elapsed-time computation bypassed the negative and NaN guard that spanMs already had from #136. The agent extracted a shared asDuration predicate, and round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: The same duration-domain gap recurred one PR after #136/F4 was fixed, because that fix guarded one producer rather than establishing a shared predicate for every duration.

evidence: The forged literal used `agent-review-cost:` instead of `agent-review-cost-usd`. The agent confirmed parseCostRecord returns null for it, so the test passed through the no-marker path. a8bc36b corrects the literal, and a mutation that deletes `&& v >= 0` now fails the test.
guidance_note: When writing a test for a guard, mutate the guard once and confirm the test fails before committing it.

evidence: The tallyQuantity comment claimed `n` was already screened by parseCostRecord, yet tallyCost passes a live figure and renderPrTime passes raw thisMs. Routing tallyQuantity through recordedQuantity enforces the reviewer's 'n >= 0' option with the single existing predicate.
guidance_note: Before writing a comment that says inputs are 'already screened', check every call site of the function, not the one you just wrote.

evidence: The signature gained `priorDuration` while the comment above it still said 'two facts' and 'two values'. a8bc36b updates it to three.
guidance_note: When adding a parameter to a function whose comment counts its parameters, update the count in the same edit.

narrative: Round 0 raised three real issues: a vacuous test caused by a marker-name typo, a comment overstating that inputs were pre-screened, and a stale parameter count. All were fixed in one commit, and the agent proved the test non-vacuous by mutation. Round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: The agent's mutation check on the fixed test is the practice that would have caught F1 before review if run when the test was first written.
